name: Hiroshima
tagline: The city that rebuilt itself on an iron griddle: layered okonomiyaki, oysters from the bay and neighbourhood counters.
history: Before the war, Hiroshima children bought issen yōshoku, 'one-sen Western food': a thin flour pancake with spring onion, folded in half. Soon after the bomb, a similar stall appeared on the black market in front of the station. Many women who had lost their husbands to the war or the bomb set up a griddle in their front room, which is why so many shops are called 'so-and-so-chan'.

With food short, cheap year-round cabbage replaced the spring onion. The batter isn't mixed with the fillings: it becomes a thin base, the cabbage is piled on top, and the whole thing is flipped and steamed under the batter. Around 1955 noodles (soba or udon) went in, and the Hiroshima style was complete. In 1950 Sasaki Shōten (now Otafuku) started making the sauce and in 1952 launched Japan's first 'okonomiyaki sauce'. The stalls on Chūō avenue became Okonomimura in 1967.

Hiroshima Bay has farmed oysters since the 16th century. Bamboo rafts from 1953 made production explode, and today the prefecture produces half to 60% of Japan's oysters. From the Edo period to the Taishō, Hiroshima's 'kaki-bune' (oyster boats) sold oysters moored on Osaka's rivers.
winter: December and January are peak oyster months (the season runs November to March). Oysters fried, grilled, in rice and on okonomiyaki. The oyster festivals around the bay start in January. We're only here on the "Full" alternative: two nights, 4–6 Jan.

meibutsu.name: Hiroshima okonomiyaki
meibutsu.what: Layers: thin batter, a mountain of cabbage, pork, noodles and egg, pressed on the griddle and topped with Otafuku sauce. You eat it off the griddle with a small spatula (hera).
meibutsu.where: Hassho, Tatsu or Denkō Sekka (in the station).
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: fine, the egg is cooked on the griddle. Avoid only raw-oyster or raw-egg toppings.
meibutsu.glance: Layered savoury pancake: batter, cabbage, pork, noodles, egg, sauce.
meibutsu.story: After the bomb, many women who had lost their husbands set up a griddle in their front room, which is why so many shops are called 'so-and-so-chan'. Hiroshima okonomiyaki is built in layers, not mixed: a thin batter base, a mountain of cabbage, pork, noodles and egg, pressed on the griddle and finished with Otafuku sauce. Eat it straight off the griddle with the little spatula, the hera.

meibutsu.name: Hiroshima oysters
meibutsu.what: Big and creamy, at their best in December. Kaki-furai (breaded and fried), grilled in the shell, in rice (kaki-meshi) or raw.
meibutsu.where: Miyajima (Yakigaki no Hayashi, Kakiya) or as an okonomiyaki topping.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: no raw oysters (生がき). Fried, grilled and in rice are all fine.
meibutsu.glance: Big, creamy bay oysters, at their best in December.
meibutsu.story: Hiroshima Bay has farmed oysters since the 16th century, and bamboo rafts from 1953 made production explode: the prefecture now grows half to 60% of Japan's oysters. From the Edo period to the Taishō, Hiroshima's oyster boats even moored on Osaka's rivers to sell them. December is peak. Have them fried as kaki-furai, grilled in the shell or cooked in rice. Fernanda skips only the raw ones.

meibutsu.name: Hiroshima tsukemen
meibutsu.what: Cold noodles to dip in a red chilli sauce; you choose how hot.
meibutsu.glance: Cold noodles dipped in red chilli sauce; you choose the heat.

meibutsu.name: Momiji manjū
meibutsu.what: A maple-leaf-shaped cake filled with anko, created on Miyajima in 1906. Everyone's Hiroshima souvenir.
meibutsu.glance: A maple-leaf cake filled with sweet bean paste, born on Miyajima.

meibutsu.name: Anago-meshi
meibutsu.what: Conger eel grilled in sauce over rice cooked in broth. The Miyajimaguchi ekiben, also sold at the station.
meibutsu.glance: Grilled conger eel over broth-cooked rice; the Miyajimaguchi bentō.
meibutsu.story: Ueno has been making anago-meshi at Miyajimaguchi since 1901. Conger eel is grilled in sauce and laid over rice cooked in broth. It's the Miyajimaguchi ekiben, the station bentō, and it's also sold at Hiroshima Station. Buy a box and eat it on the ferry to Miyajima or on the Shinkansen. It's all cooked, so it's fine for Fernanda.

meibutsu.name: Oyster okonomiyaki
meibutsu.what: Winter okonomiyaki: grilled oysters on top. The best way for Fernanda to have oysters.
meibutsu.where: Okonomiyaki counters in December and January.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: fine if well grilled; ask for よく焼いて.
meibutsu.glance: Winter okonomiyaki topped with grilled oysters; Fernanda's way in.

areas.name: Okonomimura
areas.story: A building with dozens of okonomiyaki counters over three floors, heir to the 1950 stalls. Famous, but Tabelog itself leaves Okonomimura off its 2025 list of 21 okonomiyaki places locals recommend, and the branches there sit around 3.4.
eat: Okonomiyaki at any counter, if you're nearby and hungry
areas.tips: Good to look at. To eat, go to a neighbourhood counter.
areas.dec_jan: New Year hours to confirm in early December.
areas.glance: The famous okonomiyaki building: good to look at, eat elsewhere.

areas.name: Hiroshima Station (ekie)
areas.story: The station mall has a 百名店 okonomiyaki and the prefecture's souvenirs.
areas.tips: Plan B for all seven of us on a travel day.
areas.dec_jan: Open over New Year with shorter hours (to confirm in early December). Our travel days here are 4 and 6 Jan.
areas.glance: Station mall with top-100 okonomiyaki and souvenirs; the group fallback.

areas.name: Nagarekawa and Yagenbori
areas.story: The bar and izakaya district in the centre, with okonomiyaki counters open late.
areas.dec_jan: New Year hours to confirm in early December.
areas.glance: Bar and izakaya district with okonomiyaki counters open late.

places.name: Okonomiyaki Hassho, Kanayama-chō
places.why: Cabbage steamed until sweet, thin crisp batter: the standard locals measure the others by. Yagenbori Hassho (3.70, 百名店 2025) is the older line and opens in the evening.
places.order: Soba-iri with egg; in December, with oysters.
places.group: 32 seats (20 at tables): ask for seven together, or split 4+3.
places.dec_jan: Open Wed–Sun, 10:00–17:00, so closed Mon 4 and Tue 5 Jan, our two days here; only possible on the morning of Wed 6 Jan before we leave. New Year hours to confirm in early December. Yagenbori Hassho, open in the evening, is the likelier bet (its days to check).
places.glance: The okonomiyaki locals measure all the others by.

places.name: Okonomiyaki Tatsu
places.why: The city's top score at a tiny counter with one tatami table for six, one short of us.
places.group: 9 seats: book the tatami table for 6 and ask whether a seventh fits, or seat one at the counter.
places.dec_jan: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays: 4 and 5 Jan, our two Hiroshima days. Only possible on 6 Jan before the train, if it's open then; New Year hours to confirm in early December.
places.glance: The city's top okonomiyaki score, at a tiny counter.

places.name: Denkō Sekka ekie
places.why: The easy option on a train day: a 百名店, inside the station, with space for the group. (≈2,000 reviews.)
places.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: ask for the egg well cooked (よく焼いて).
places.group: 50 seats: room for all seven, maybe over two tables.
places.dec_jan: New Year hours to confirm in early December. In the station, so it's the fallback on 4 and 6 Jan, our travel days.

critics.note: Went once (Nov 2019), according to the City Foodsters visit log.

places.glance: Easy top-100 okonomiyaki inside the station, with room for everyone.

shops.name: Otafuku (sauce)
shops.what: The okonomiyaki sauce created in Hiroshima in 1952.
shops.buy: A bottle of sauce to make it at home.

shops.name: Anagomeshi Ueno (bentō)
shops.what: Anago-meshi to take away, made since 1901.
shops.buy: A bentō for the ferry or the Shinkansen.
shops.dec_jan: No fixed day off. New Year hours to confirm in early December.
